_note: The spend plane's platform-neutral laws (architecture/proposals/cost-guardrails.md). Three sections: `windows` pins the window arithmetic (hour/day epoch-aligned, month = UTC calendar month — two isolates must agree which window a unit belongs to, and a monthly ceiling must reset when a human expects it to); `resolution` pins which budget meters which kind (exact match everywhere except egress, which uses the egress gate's own suffix rule so allowlist and meter can never disagree — and the lookalike-suffix attack the gate refuses, the meter must refuse too); `verdicts` pins the ceiling behaviour itself (counting under `unbounded`, the 80% warning fired once, the trip strictly past `max`, the roll re-opening the breaker). Executed by OpenSource/Web/packages/server/test/spend.test.ts; the plane runs on the one server runtime, so this corpus has a single runner by design (the same standing as ai/mcp/server-transport.json).

windows.name: hour aligns to the epoch hour
hour at an exact boundary starts its own window
day aligns to the epoch day
day zero is the epoch itself
month is the UTC calendar month
month across a year boundary rolls to January
february of a leap year ends on March 1

resolution.name: a data kind resolves exactly, never across planes
an egress budget meters its exact host
an egress budget meters subdomains of its host
a lookalike suffix does not match — the gate's own attack case
among nested egress declarations the MOST SPECIFIC host wins, whatever the order
a host outside the specific declaration still falls to the broad one

verdicts.name: under the ceiling every charge is allowed and nothing transitions
the ceiling itself is still allowed; strictly past it is the trip
a tripped budget refuses every further charge and keeps counting
unbounded counts and never refuses and never transitions
the window rolling re-opens a tripped budget and announces the recovery
